Alwin Wren.narrative: I have lived by the chapel wall longer than most of the town can remember, and I have buried fewer people than the sisters fear I might. I know which root stops a fever and which one only makes the dying quieter, and I charge nothing for either — the poor have no marks, and the rich have no need of me. The Reeve does not send for me, which suits me; the sisters still come to my door when their salves fail. I keep my own fire and my own counsel, and I do not bow at the gate.
values: the poor deserve healing as much as the rich
a healer's hands should be free of price
the town's peace is worth more than its pride
goals: keep the poor of Brackenford alive through the winter
be left alone to keep my books and my garden
see the gate-due lifted so the roads are open again
to teach Pernel Pip enough of the herbs that the knowledge will not die with me
to walk the woods by the stone road once more before the cold, and come home with my basket full

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: She has more sense than the rest of the chapel put together, and she knows when to look the other way.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: Eager, and her garden is better than her dosing — she will learn.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: Keeps the fire well enough, but she counts the feast days and not the people.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: A man who weighs grain and never weighs what a due costs the carrier.

relations.name: Hilda Smith
relations.label: fellow healer
relations.note: Sets bones clean; we send each other the cases we cannot mend alone.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: Steady hands at a birth, and she does not chatter about it after.

relations.name: Pernel Pip
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: The girl lodges with the sisters and writes my letters for me when my hand shakes.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I set her boy's fever and asked nothing; what she does on the road is her own business.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: I made broth from nettles and bones for half the town and watched the children's cheeks come back.
A gate guard's leg went bad after a wolf bite; I cut and burned and he lived, and the Reeve never thanked me.
Sister Elspeth came to my door at midnight for a salve for the chapel's common fire burn, and stayed to argue herbs with me till dawn.
I walked to Coldwell last winter to a boy with a fever, and came back through the woods with wolves singing behind me.
My mother taught me the charm for a stopped breath by the light of one candle, and made me say it until I could say it in my sleep.

stances.why: the poor have no marks and a healer who charges them is no healer
it taxes the sick and the hungry on their way to be helped
they were good enough for my mother and they work
the Reeve and the Guild can quarrel without my name in it
Elspeth has never once betrayed a confidence of mine

Alwin Wren.secret: I keep a book of old charms and heathen words my mother left me, hidden under the floor by the hearth; the chapel would call it wicked if they knew.
pastimes: tending the herb garden along the chapel wall
reading and annotating the old books of roots and remedies
sitting by the common fire in the evening, listening to the town's talk
Alwin Wren.calling: I gather and know the roots that heal, and I give them freely to those who cannot pay.
